A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Control-GIC. The main text, all 13 figures, three tables, and Appendices A.1–A.7 are readable and support comparison. The shorter v4 reflects reformatting rather than missing appendix material.

before.justification: v3 reports original compression benchmarks, efficiency measurements, decoder ablations, and qualitative experiments, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark and appendix results and reports a revised entropy-coding comparison in Table 1.

M1.justification: Equation (6) removes the reconstruction-loss multiplier β, and Section 3.4 deletes the statement about tuning it. This changes the stated objective, although the PDFs do not establish whether training changed. The encoder, conditional decoder, and entropy-coding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on OpenImages and evaluate on Kodak, DIV2K, and CLIC2020. The small-face examples and extremely low-bitrate scenarios already appear in v3 and are retained in v4.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes ZIP as an entropy-coding comparator, retaining uniform-frequency Huffman coding. The comparator sets in the main benchmarks and the appendix comparison with Mao et al. remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces granularity percentages (0,50,50), (10,80,10), and (50,40,10) with (100,0,0), (60,30,10), and (20,50,30). These are revised entropy-coding evaluation settings. The training data, budget, and hardware reported in Section 4.1 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The entropy-coding component analysis in Section 4.3 is revised through different granularity settings and removal of the ZIP comparison. The bitrate-control analysis, decoder-condition ablations, and granularity/small-face case studies in Figures 7–9 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The use of FID and KID remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the earlier results and reported Huffman-relative savings of 6.4%, 6.6%, and 8.2% with 5.0%, 2.9%, and 0.4%. Because the granularity settings differ, these are replacement results rather than same-setting performance declines. Benchmark curves, Tables 2–3, and reconstruction examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 removes the expanded bitrate derivations from v3 Equation (12). Its mask-cost equality was algebraically inconsistent; v4 retains only the final expression (4r1+r2)/256 as Equation (13), removing that inconsistency. The spatial-entropy definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a single controllable compression model, granularity-based bitrate allocation, statistical entropy coding, and a probabilistic conditional decoder.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reconstruction characterization from 'nearly lossless' to 'nearly minimal-loss.' Appendix A.6 removes the qualification that Mao et al.'s comparison numbers were approximated from their paper. The small-face limitation in Appendix A.4 remains.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository link in the abstract. It removes the CDC setting ρ=0.9 from Section 4.2, the Kodak 192-patch FID/KID detail from Appendix A.1, and the explanation of unavailable Mao code/models and paper-derived baseline numbers from Appendix A.6.

R1.justification: The bibliography and overall research positioning remain unchanged. Section 2 corrects attribution to the already cited Toderici et al. (2016), without expanding the literature coverage or changing the novelty argument.

P1.justification: v4 corrects terminology such as 'adaption,' edits grammar, rewrites explanations in Appendices A.2–A.4 and A.6, and adds acknowledgments and publication-status text. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adopts ICLR formatting and reflows existing figures. Table 1 replaces the ZIP column with a savings column; Figure 2 gains a frequency-distribution label, and Figure 9 gains panel labels. Captions are edited, and appendix image panels are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: v4 improves wording, adds code-access information, and removes local inconsistencies in Figure 7 and Appendix A.3. However, it loses baseline configuration and provenance disclosures, especially the qualification of Mao et al.'s approximated results. The unexplained β removal also leaves its relationship to the retained experiments unresolved. These competing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
